# WARDROBE DAY — shared client records

## Product and audience

- Product name: WARDROBE DAY.
- Audience: young adults managing existing garments, exploring personal style and planning outfits for everyday occasions.
- Product activities: manual garment entry and editing; wardrobe browsing; outfit assembly and saving; occasion planning; availability and conflict review.
- Supplied content: seven garment images, entered garment fields, outfit memberships, occasions, preferences and one planning outlook.
- Record labels: human-readable garment, outfit and event names.
- Internal IDs: source-record identifiers; optional discreet interface metadata.
- Navigation alternatives: garment-led, outfit-led and occasion-led.

## Display and fixed wording

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Phone orientation | Portrait |
| Phone logical canvas | 402 × 874 pt |
| Phone safe areas | Top 62 pt; bottom 34 pt; left 0 pt; right 0 pt |
| Tablet orientation | Landscape |
| Tablet logical canvas | 1024 × 768 pt |
| Tablet safe areas | Top, bottom, left and right 24 pt |
| Interface platform | Platform-neutral |
| Main wardrobe identity | WARDROBE DAY |
| Main wardrobe total | 7 items |
| Reference-time available count | 5 available |
| Outfit-saving action | Save outfit |
| Plan-confirmation action | Confirm plan |
| Availability labels | Available; In laundry; Loaned |
| Weather context label | Planning outlook |
| Body-text contrast | At least 4.5:1 |
| Large-text and meaningful-icon contrast | At least 3:1 |
| Status expression | Colour plus text and symbols |
| Component states | Default; pressed; disabled; error |
| Outer-layer suggestion states | Suggested; awaiting confirmation; applied |

## Image identity

- Garment records: seven, including two matching footwear pairs.
- Footwear counting unit: one matching pair equals one wardrobe record.
- Identity sources: t01.png, t02.png, b01.png, b02.png, f01.png, f02.png, j01.png.
- Fixed visual attributes: each item's colour, construction, garment parts, orientation and existing surface details.
- Final garment representations: supplied original images, with uniform scaling, rectangular framing that retains identifying construction, or background removal around the intact item.
- Process representations: source images or labelled placeholders.
- Outfit memberships: unarranged data; composition layout and navigation remain open.
- Garment material, fit and performance properties: unspecified beyond the visible descriptions in the register.

## Reference time and interval rules

- Reference time: Monday 14 September 2026, 08:00, UTC+08:00.
- Calendar time zone: UTC+08:00 for all displayed dates and times.
- Unavailable windows: start-inclusive, end-exclusive.
- T02 unavailable through the interval ending 14 September 2026, 18:00.
- B02 unavailable through the interval ending 15 September 2026, 12:00.
- Reference-time available records: T01, B01, F01, F02, J01; count 5.
- Future-event availability basis: overlap between the proposed event interval and each item's recorded unavailable intervals.
- Item-detail history: original laundry and loan records remain attached to the garment after planning.

## Outfit and reservation rules

- Complete planning membership: exactly one top, one bottom and one footwear record; one outerwear record optional.
- Incomplete membership: editable draft; plan confirmation disabled.
- Saved outfit membership: available and currently unavailable garments permitted.
- Viewing and editing saved outfits: available regardless of current garment availability.
- Unavailable garment overlapping the proposed event: blocked confirmation; editable draft retained with its members and original availability records.
- Reservation conflict: a shared garment ID and overlapping confirmed-event intervals.
- Touching interval endpoints: compatible reservations.
- Different outfit names with shared garments: the same interval-overlap rule.
- Conflict information: affected garment names, conflicting event name and time, retained draft, garment-editing route or explicitly permitted alternative time.
- Fixed events and existing plans: their recorded times and memberships persist through the Rain walk flow.
- Garment laundry and loan state after outfit use: original records persist until a separate manual change.

## Preferences and outlook

- User preference: reuse existing garments and review conflicts before confirmation.
- Repeat-wear advice: enabled.
- Repeat condition: identical complete garment set on a different date within the preceding seven calendar days.
- Repeat effect: advisory; acknowledgement permits continuation.
- Same-date reuse in non-overlapping intervals: outside the repeat-advice condition.
- Outer-layer preference: dismissible suggestion for the supplied light-rain outlook.
- Outerwear membership: optional.
- Outer-layer interaction: suggestion, user confirmation pending, then applied after manual jacket addition; dismissal is available.
- Planning outlook date: Monday 14 September 2026.
- Planning outlook temperature: 18°C.
- Planning outlook condition: light rain.
- Weather context: supplied planning outlook for this date.
- Garment performance: unspecified.

| F01 | White low-top sneakers | f01.png | footwear | white | One matching pair, low tops, laces and rubber soles | available | One pair is one wardrobe record. | None recorded |
| F02 | Black penny loafers | f02.png | footwear | black | One matching black leather-look pair, low heels and simple penny straps | available | One pair is one wardrobe record. | None recorded |
| J01 | Olive hooded jacket | j01.png | outerwear | olive green | Lightweight appearance, attached hood, front zip and two lower front pockets | available | Optional outer layer; waterproof performance unspecified. | None recorded |

## Main interaction snapshots

| Main calendar after confirmation | E01 with O01; E02 with O03; E03 with O02 | E01 14 September 09:00–10:00; E02 14 September 11:00–12:00; E03 16 September 14:00–15:00 |

## Additional recorded states

| T01 discard confirmation | Unsaved Steam collar before use. replacing Hang after wearing. | Dialog choices: keep editing or discard; discard outcome restores original note and retains saved outfits, calendar and garment identity |

## Compact state-components examples

| Search zero results | purple; zero matches; clear-query action |

| Repeat advisory | E04; O01 set previously used by E01 on 14 September; acknowledgement and continuation |
| Discard dialog | T01 unsaved note; keep editing or discard |
| Successful confirmation | O03 and E02 at 11:00–12:00; default and pressed Confirm plan component samples |

- Example grouping: six separate labelled groups.
- Interface entity states: unsaved draft; saved outfit; confirmed calendar plan.
- Expanded views: additional instances of wardrobe browsing, garment editing, outfit editing, calendar planning and existing feedback states.

steps.userMessage:
WARDROBE DAY | A personal wardrobe and everyday outfit planner

We are commissioning WARDROBE DAY for young adults who want to use the clothes they already own and decide what to wear before the day begins. The app connects a seven-item wardrobe, saved outfits and everyday occasions. Garment images and fields are supplied; adding and editing garments are manual actions. Each footwear pair counts as one item. At Monday 14 September 2026, 08:00, UTC+08:00, five items are available; Cream knit sweater is in laundry until 18:00 that day, and Indigo straight jeans is loaned until Tuesday 15 September at 12:00. Print "WARDROBE DAY", "7 items" and "5 available" on the main wardrobe screen. Use "Save outfit" for saving an outfit and "Confirm plan" for committing it to an occasion. Availability labels are "Available", "In laundry" and "Loaned". Navigation and visual direction are open.

The central task is planning Rain walk for Coffee catch-up. Its unsaved draft contains Navy Oxford shirt, Charcoal straight trousers, White low-top sneakers and Olive hooded jacket. The initial 09:30–10:30 time overlaps Studio review at 09:00–10:00; the shirt and trousers are the two reserved items. The user chooses the permitted 11:00–12:00 alternative, saves Rain walk and confirms Coffee catch-up. A complete outfit has one top, one bottom and one footwear record, with optional outerwear. Availability is assessed over the occasion's interval. The planning outlook for 14 September is 18°C and light rain; label it "Planning outlook" beside the dismissible outer-layer suggestion, with distinct suggested, awaiting-confirmation and applied states. Use platform-neutral phone screens at a logical 402 × 874 pt, with top and bottom safe areas of 62 pt and 34 pt. Landscape tablet screens, where a delivery section requests them, use 1024 × 768 pt with 24 pt safe areas on all four sides. Body text contrast is at least 4.5:1; large text and meaningful icons are at least 3:1. Availability and feedback combine colour with text and symbols.

Audience: the product owner and interface engineering team, deciding the first-release navigation and the editing-to-calendar interaction.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the garment register, outfit memberships, event records, preferences and interaction states. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists each deliverable's proportion, format and stage. phone-safe-area.png is the constraint drawing for the phone canvas and safe areas. tablet-safe-area.png is the constraint drawing for the tablet canvas and safe areas. t01.png is the fixed identity image for Navy Oxford shirt. t02.png is the fixed identity image for Cream knit sweater. b01.png is the fixed identity image for Charcoal straight trousers. b02.png is the fixed identity image for Indigo straight jeans. f01.png is the fixed identity image for the White low-top sneakers pair. f02.png is the fixed identity image for the Black penny loafers pair. j01.png is the fixed identity image for Olive hooded jacket. wardrobe-planning-scene.png provides atmosphere reference for choosing clothes beside a calendar.

Deliverables:
1. Three comparison boards, one each for garment-led, outfit-led and occasion-led navigation, each tracing wardrobe access through outfit editing to a calendar plan and proposing a distinct visual direction
2. One two-page selection and interaction specification recording the chosen direction, a page × entry × data table for the phone and tablet views, and a component × state × value table covering default, pressed, disabled and error states, with colour values and contrast ratios
3. Two phone wardrobe screens: the complete seven-item wardrobe with manual garment entry, and its five-item available-only filter
4. Three phone garment screens: Cream knit sweater detail with its laundry record, Indigo straight jeans detail with its loan record, and the unsaved Navy Oxford shirt note edit
5. Three phone outfit-editor screens: Rain walk D03 with the applied jacket suggestion, incomplete D04 with missing footwear, and complete D05 with Cream knit sweater unavailable for the proposed time
6. Two phone calendar screens: the calendar after confirmation with Studio review, Coffee catch-up and Bookshop afternoon, and the empty Thursday 17 September day with an occasion-creation action
7. Two phone outfit-detail screens: saved Rain walk with Coffee catch-up at 11:00–12:00, and Easy weekend with Bookshop afternoon on 16 September at 14:00–15:00
8. One finished state-components sheet with six labelled groups: availability badges, purple search zero results, the D03 reservation block, the E04 repeat advisory, the T01 discard dialog and successful O03/E02 confirmation
9. Three phone planning-state screens: the D03 reservation conflict, successful Rain walk confirmation after the explicit time change, and the Navy weekday repeat preview for Portfolio coffee
10. Two landscape tablet applications of the selected system: the complete wardrobe and the calendar after confirmation
11. One 12-second flow video using the delivered editor, conflict, confirmation and calendar screens, ending on the tablet calendar
12. One presentation document of at least ten pages, reusing the three comparisons, selection, specification, phone and tablet screens and state components

Acceptance:
- The three comparison boards precede the selection and interaction specification's explicit choice. The specification records the chosen landing-page name, primary-action colour code, page names and Available / In laundry / Loaned labels; the phone and tablet wardrobe and calendar screens repeat that system, and the presentation's first page repeats the choice, landing-page name and colour code.
- Both complete wardrobe screens print WARDROBE DAY, 7 items and 5 available. The filtered wardrobe contains exactly T01, B01, F01, F02 and J01 while retaining the seven-item total. The sweater and jeans details retain their recorded laundry and loan intervals, ending 14 September at 18:00 and 15 September at 12:00 respectively. The shirt-edit screen changes only "Hang after wearing." to unsaved "Steam collar before use."; all garment screens preserve the seven supplied identities.
- The D03 editor and reservation screen retain T01 + B01 + F01 + J01 and identify exactly T01 and B01 as reserved by Studio review at 09:00–10:00. D04 contains T01 + B01 and identifies missing footwear. D05 contains T02 + B01 + F01 and identifies the sweater's laundry end at 18:00 against the proposed 11:00–12:00 appointment. All three blocked states disable Confirm plan and retain editable drafts. The D03 editor carries Planning outlook, 18°C, light rain and the applied jacket suggestion; its suggested and awaiting-confirmation states appear in the specification and state-components sheet.
- The confirmation screen and video show the explicit change to 11:00–12:00, followed by saved Rain walk and confirmed Coffee catch-up, with Save outfit and Confirm plan serving their named actions. Both populated calendars, Rain walk detail and the presentation agree on that result and preserve Studio review with Navy weekday on 14 September, 09:00–10:00, and Bookshop afternoon with Easy weekend on 16 September, 14:00–15:00. Easy weekend detail contains T02 + B02 + F01 and shows availability for its future occasion. The empty-day screen identifies Thursday 17 September and offers occasion creation.
- The state-components sheet contains its six named groups and repeats the specification's default, pressed, disabled and error values. Its purple search offers query clearing, and its discard dialog offers continued editing or restoration of the original shirt note. The repeat-preview screen and sheet identify the identical Navy weekday set from 14 September for Portfolio coffee on 15 September, 18:00–19:00, as an advisory awaiting acknowledgement. The presentation reuses these examples and the three availability labels.
- All 15 phone screens use 402 × 874 pt with 62 pt top / 34 pt bottom safe areas; both tablet screens use 1024 × 768 pt with 24 pt safe areas on all sides. Their controls follow the specification's state values, with body text at least 4.5:1, large text and icons at least 3:1, and status labels and symbols accompanying colour. The video lasts 12 seconds and finishes on the delivered tablet calendar; the presentation has at least ten pages.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
